prompt: Write three short paragraphs about the sea, nothing else.

text: The user just wants three short paragraphs about the sea, nothing more — I'll keep my response focused on that alone.

The sea covers most of the planet and holds most of its water. From the shore it looks simple, a flat line where blue meets sky, but under the surface it runs miles deep, through trenches and mountain ranges no one has ever seen. Sunlight gives out a few hundred meters down, and below that is a cold, dark world we still know little about.

The sea is never still. Tides rise and fall with the pull of the moon, currents carry warm water from the equator toward the poles, and wind pushes up waves that can cross whole oceans before they break on some far-off beach. That steady motion shapes coastlines, spreads heat around the Earth, and keeps the weather turning.

People have always been drawn to it. Sailors have crossed it for trade and discovery, fishers have made their living from it, and poets have used it to stand for longing, danger and things without end. Standing at the edge of the water, many of us feel small, and that feeling, oddly, is part of what pulls us back.
